theory.overview: Backtracking is a systematic way to explore all possible solutions by building candidates incrementally and abandoning candidates that cannot lead to valid solutions (pruning). It's essentially depth-first search with pruning. Used for combinatorial problems: permutations, combinations, subsets, N-Queens, Sudoku, etc. This chapter covers backtracking patterns, pruning techniques, and classic backtracking problems.

sections.title: Backtracking Pattern
sections.content: Define state (current partial solution). Base case: if complete, record solution. Recursive case: try all valid choices, recurse, backtrack (undo choice). Pruning: skip choices that cannot lead to solution. Time complexity: often exponential, but pruning reduces search space.
sections.pattern: def backtrack(state): if complete: record; return; for choice in valid_choices(state): make_choice(state, choice); backtrack(state); undo_choice(state, choice);
sections.complexity: Exponential in worst case, pruning helps

sections.title: Permutations
sections.content: Generate all permutations of array. State: current permutation, used elements. For each unused element, add to permutation, recurse, remove. Time: $O(n! \times n)$. Space: $O(n)$ for recursion stack.
sections.algorithm: For each position, try each unused element. Recurse. Backtrack by marking unused.

sections.title: Combinations
sections.content: Generate all combinations of k elements from n. State: current combination, start index. Only consider elements from start index onward (avoid duplicates). Time: $O(C(n,k) \times k)$. Space: $O(k)$.
sections.algorithm: For i from start to n-k+len(combination): add nums[i], recurse with i+1, remove.

sections.title: Subsets
sections.content: Generate all subsets (power set). State: current subset, index. For each element, two choices: include or exclude. Time: $O(2^n \times n)$. Space: $O(n)$. Can also generate iteratively.
sections.algorithm: For each index, two branches: include nums[i] or exclude. Recurse to next index.

sections.title: Pruning Techniques
sections.content: Early termination: stop if current partial cannot lead to solution. Constraint checking: only make valid choices. Ordering: process choices in promising order first. Memoization: cache subproblem results to avoid recomputation. These techniques dramatically reduce search space.

keyConcepts.name: State
keyConcepts.description: Current partial solution. Must capture all information needed to continue search.
keyConcepts.example: Current permutation, used elements set, current position

keyConcepts.name: Backtrack
keyConcepts.description: Undo choice after recursion to restore state for next iteration. Essential for exploring all possibilities.
keyConcepts.action: Remove element, unmark used, decrement index

keyConcepts.name: Pruning
keyConcepts.description: Skip branches that cannot lead to valid solution. Reduces exponential search space.

keyConcepts.name: Base Case
keyConcepts.description: Condition when partial solution is complete. Record solution and return.
keyConcepts.check: Permutation length = n, combination length = k, etc.

steps.title: Define State
steps.description: Define what represents current partial solution (array, index, used set, etc.).

steps.title: Base Case
steps.description: Check if current solution is complete. If yes, record and return.

steps.title: Generate Choices
steps.description: Generate all valid choices from current state.

steps.title: Make Choice and Recurse
steps.description: Apply choice, recurse, then backtrack (undo choice).

practiceProblems.title: Subsets
practiceProblems.description: Generate all subsets (power set) of array.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack: for each element, include or exclude. Or iterative: start with [[]], for each num, add to all existing subsets.

practiceProblems.title: Subsets II
practiceProblems.description: Generate all subsets with duplicates (no duplicate subsets).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort array. Skip duplicates at same level: if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1], skip.
practiceProblems.hints: Sort, skip duplicates at same level

practiceProblems.title: Permutations
practiceProblems.description: Generate all permutations of array.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack with used set. For each unused element, add, recurse, remove.

practiceProblems.title: Permutations II
practiceProblems.description: Generate all permutations with duplicates (no duplicate permutations).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort array. Skip duplicates: if used[i] or (i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i-1] and not used[i-1]), skip.
practiceProblems.hints: Sort, skip duplicates with used check

practiceProblems.title: Combinations
practiceProblems.description: Generate all combinations of k elements from 1 to n.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack with start index. Only consider elements from start onward.

practiceProblems.title: Combination Sum
practiceProblems.description: Find all combinations that sum to target (unlimited use of candidates).
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. Start from each candidate, recurse with remaining target. Allow reuse by not incrementing index.

practiceProblems.title: Combination Sum II
practiceProblems.description: Find combinations that sum to target (each candidate used once, duplicates in candidates).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort candidates. Skip duplicates at same level. Increment index to avoid reuse.

practiceProblems.title: Palindrome Partitioning
practiceProblems.description: Partition string into substrings that are all palindromes.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. For each position, try all substrings starting there. If palindrome, add and recurse.

practiceProblems.title: Letter Combinations of Phone Number
practiceProblems.description: Generate all letter combinations for phone number digits.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. For each digit, try all corresponding letters.

practiceProblems.title: N-Queens
practiceProblems.description: Place n queens on n×n chessboard so no two attack each other.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack row by row. Check column and diagonals for conflicts.

practiceProblems.title: N-Queens II
practiceProblems.description: Count number of distinct solutions to N-Queens.
practiceProblems.solution: Same as N-Queens but count instead of return solutions.

practiceProblems.title: Sudoku Solver
practiceProblems.description: Solve Sudoku puzzle.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. Find empty cell, try digits 1-9, check validity, recurse.

practiceProblems.title: Word Search
practiceProblems.description: Check if word exists in board (can move in 4 directions, each cell once).
practiceProblems.solution: DFS/backtrack from each cell. Mark visited, unmark on backtrack.

practiceProblems.title: Restore IP Addresses
practiceProblems.description: Restore all valid IP addresses from string.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. Try placing dots at valid positions (0-255, no leading zeros unless 0).

practiceProblems.title: Generate Parentheses
practiceProblems.description: Generate all combinations of n pairs of well-formed parentheses.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. Track open and close count. Add '(' if open < n, add ')' if close < open.

practiceProblems.title: Word Search II
practiceProblems.description: Find all words from dictionary in board.
practiceProblems.solution: Trie + backtracking. Build Trie from dictionary. DFS from each cell, traverse Trie.

practiceProblems.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
practiceProblems.description: Check if array can be partitioned into k subsets with equal sum.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtracking with memoization. Sort descending for better pruning.

practiceProblems.title: Split Array into Fibonacci Sequence
practiceProblems.description: Check if array can be split into Fibonacci sequence.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. Try all possible first two numbers, check if rest follows Fibonacci.

practiceProblems.title: Beautiful Arrangement
practiceProblems.description: Count beautiful arrangements (nums[i] divisible by i+1 or vice versa).
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. At position i, try all unused numbers that satisfy condition.

practiceProblems.title: Binary Watch
practiceProblems.description: Return all possible times given number of LEDs lit.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack or iterate all 10 bits combinations. Check valid time.

practiceProblems.title: Gray Code
practiceProblems.description: Generate n-bit Gray code sequence.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack or iterative: G(n) = G(n-1) + reverse(G(n-1)) with leading bit.
practiceProblems.hints: Recursive: add 0 to G(n-1), add 1 to reverse

practiceProblems.title: Strobogrammatic Number II
practiceProblems.description: Find all strobogrammatic numbers of length n.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. Build from outside in. Valid pairs: 0-0, 1-1, 6-9, 8-8, 9-6.

practiceProblems.title: Generalized Abbreviation
practiceProblems.description: Generate all possible abbreviations of word.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. For each position, either keep character or abbreviate (count consecutive abbreviations).

practiceProblems.title: Expression Add Operators
practiceProblems.description: Add operators (+, -, *) to make expression equal target.
practiceProblems.solution: Backtrack. Track current value, previous operand, and expression string.

practiceProblems.title: Word Squares
practiceProblems.description: Find all word squares (k×k grid where row i = column i as words).
practiceProblems.solution: Trie + backtracking. Build square row by row, use Trie to validate prefixes.

minigame.title: Backtracking Master
minigame.description: Master backtracking! Permutations, combinations, N-Queens, and Sudoku.

visualizer.description: Visualize backtracking: state tree, pruning, and solution exploration.
